units.translation: where in M χνόαί [the axle-ends] with double accent. The correct accent is attested by Herodian in Arcadius p. 108, 13 and in the scholia on Sophocles El. 711. On the meaning, the scholiast on this passage of Aeschylus says: χνόαι δὲ τὰ ἀκραξόνια, περὶ ἃ αἱ χοινικίδες οἱ παραξονῖται λεγόμενοι [the axle-ends are the tips of the axle, around which are the bushings called paraxonitai]. It therefore signifies that part of the axle which is inserted into the hub or hole of the wheel: see Thes. vol. 8 p. 1540.

Improperly, where the scholiast said μεταφορικῶς εἶπε τὰ ἄκρα τῶν ποδῶν [metaphorically he called the tips of the feet], and another said: τὸ συνεχές κίνημα τῶν ποδῶν παραβόλως χνόας εἶπεν· τοῦ μέντοι ἄξονος τὸ ἄκρον τὸ ἐντιθέμενον τῇ χοινικίδι χνόη καλεῖται [he called the continuous movement of the feet, by a bold metaphor, axle-ends; but the tip of the axle that is inserted into the bushing is called chnoē].
The axle-ends of the heavy-laden axles creaked,
eagerly pursuing the speeding axle-ends of his feet,
